venue_evaluation.downtown_linden_corner: Cafe, $. Meat-free board (grain bowl, lentil soup, falafel, stew), fresh and light, peanut-allergic diner has eaten the whole menu safely, oat latte by default, olive oil instead of butter, bean-thickened soup. Meets every constraint: 3 stars.
venue_evaluation.downtown_slate_window: Satay dressing on every grain bowl and in-house roasted peanuts. Deal-breaker for Cyrus.
venue_evaluation.downtown_wren_house: Every dish has meat or fish; vegetarian flatmate left with only coffee. Deal-breaker for Mina.
venue_evaluation.downtown_paper_kite: Peanut-free (sunflower-seed butter), half the board vegetarian, light. But heavy dairy (feta, cheddar, butter, cream, whole milk). Roxy's intolerance costs a star: 2 stars.
venue_evaluation.downtown_marble_steps: Peanut-safe, meat-free fry-up, dairy-free. But deep-fried and heavy, misses Brooke's wholesome request: 2 stars.

notes: Fair puzzle with two good decoys: Paper Kite (fails only the dairy intolerance) and Marble Steps (fails only the wholesome preference). Each costs exactly one star, so a player who misses one clue still lands on 2 stars, which feels right.

Mina's vegetarian diet is never stated outright; it comes from the sushi-day memory ('whole section with zero meat', 'order whatever looked good without asking'). That is a fair inference but the subtlest clue in the level. 'Then sushi day is today's standard' could also be read as a craving for sushi by a careless player, though all venues are cafes so it does no harm.

Paper Kite's 'half the board is meat-free' vs Mina's 'order whatever looked good without asking' raises a small question: does a half-meat menu fail her diet? I treated it as passing the diet (she has plenty to eat) and scored Paper Kite on the dairy star only. Either way it is not the best pick.

Linden Corner's peanut safety is shown indirectly (a peanut-allergic deskmate has eaten the whole menu without using her auto-injector). Clear enough, and nicely paired with the oat-latte and olive-oil details for dairy.
Cyrus's peanut allergy is well signposted by the pen plus satay plus Roxy's 'nothing satay-adjacent' echo. Slate Window is an obvious trap once seen.
Nothing contradictory found. Budget is a non-factor since every venue is $.
